newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lamassoure confirms 60 bln Ffr 1997 spend saving.
newsitem.headline: Lamassoure confirms 60 bln Ffr 1997 spend saving.

text.p: French government spokesman Alain Lamassoure confirmed there would be "cuts" of 60 billion francs in central government spending in France's 1997 budget.
He said the number of civil service posts would be reduced this year by "around 6,000" as part of the savings and that this included a net reduction of 2,590 in state education staff.

Central government spending next year is to be frozen at the 1996 level of 1,552 billion francs, but inflation and mechanical increments meant this freeze actually implied finding 60 billion francs of spending cuts or other savings.

"The savings achieved are considerable," Lamassoure said in a news conference address. "They amount to 60 billion francs compared to the level of spending that simply repeating last year's budget would have involved."
Apart from civil service staff slimming, Lamassoure said that reducing job subsidies would save 15 billion francs and stabilising EU budget contributions would save nine billion francs.
